report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of 3 of daedalus/structcore/slice.py: contains assemble logic with budget trimming, and main() CLI entry point.
risks: line 561-567 | low | Comment claims byte-identical to old flat join when max_tokens=None, but the code adds 'withheld_lines' and marker=None which may differ from old join; uncheckable without old code.
line 573-575 | medium | marker uses newline and '# ===== CONTEXT TRIMMED...' which may not be visible in all contexts; could break downstream parsing.
line 591-598 | low | Comment claims shell_boundary_stops distinguishes between 'stopped at boundary' and 'no neighbors', but this is a design claim not testable from this chunk.
line 603-609 | medium | Comment about whole_repo_tokens_exact and tokenizer honesty; the logic in main() uses 'heuristic' in tk string which is fragile; uncheckable without index structure.

handoff.purpose: Assemble slice with optional budget trimming and provide CLI entry point.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry point; writes slice text and/or JSON to disk via --out and --json.

claims.text: With max_tokens=None this is byte-identical to the old flat join;
claims.why: The old flat join is not present in this chunk; cannot verify byte-identity.

claims.text: over budget it drops WHOLE neighbour units (never truncates) and appends a visible TRIMMED marker, keeping FOCUS + WITHHELD.
claims.why: Code calls _fit_budget (which presumably drops whole neighbors) and appends marker with 'CONTEXT TRIMMED' message; focus and withheld are kept via _assemble_slice arguments.

claims.text: Edges that pointed OUT of the declared center and were therefore not expanded through. Reported rather than dropped in silence: a slice that stops at the shell boundary and a slice with no neighbors at all look identical from the outside, and only one of them is complete.
claims.why: The variable shell_stops is not defined or assigned in this chunk; its content and behavior cannot be verified.

claims.text: Files that carried secret markers / non-allow-listed egress and were therefore withheld from the slice. sorted(); each entry names the rule that fired. Empty list on a clean slice.
claims.why: The variable 'withheld' is not defined in this chunk; its value and sorting cannot be verified.

claims.text: False => the index predates total_tokens, so the denominator fell back to the chars/4 whole-repo estimate rather than the per-file token sum. True only means 'same tokenizer as the numerator', NOT 'tiktoken-measured' -- when tiktoken is absent both sides are chars/4 and the ratio is consistent but the absolute count is a heuristic. Read whole_repo_tokenizer for the honest label; a degraded tokenizer is reported there, never silent.
claims.why: The value of whole_exact is not computed in this chunk; the index structure and tokenizer logic are external.

claims.text: Honest label: name the actual tokenizer instead of blanket 'measured'. whole_repo_tokens_exact only says the denominator is the per-file token sum (not the legacy chars/4 whole-repo fallback); it does NOT say a real BPE tokenizer was used. tokenizer_name() already distinguishes the two.
claims.why: The tokenizer_name() function and index structure are not present; cannot verify the labeling logic.

claims.text: tiktoken absent: per-file chars/4 sum. Consistent with the numerator, but a heuristic -- do not call it 'measured'.
claims.why: The condition depends on 'heuristic' in tk string; the tokenizer naming convention is not verifiable from this chunk.

observations.what: The comment on lines 561-562 claims byte-identical behavior when max_tokens=None, but the code includes 'withheld_lines' and a marker of None which may differ from a hypothetical old flat join. Cannot verify.
The marker string includes a newline and '#' which is intended to be visible in the slice text; this may affect downstream parsing or display.
The code uses variables 'shell_stops' and 'withheld' that are not defined in this chunk; they must be defined earlier in the function or imported.
The main() function writes files via Path.write_text; no error handling for write failures is present.
The tokenizer labeling in main() uses string matching on 'heuristic' to decide the label; this is fragile to changes in tokenizer name strings.
